blocks.p: TRAMPTO applies a SHA-256 cryptographic seal to your documents and generates a unique digital fingerprint. From that moment on, your document is unique on the internet: no two are alike. If anyone modifies a single bit, the fingerprint no longer matches and the change is detected instantly.

We guarantee that the content hasn't changed and who sealed it and when: every seal carries a unique Seal ID, the date and the account that created it. It's complementary to e-signatures like DocuSign.
Freelancers and SMBs who need to protect quotes, contracts, invoices or deliverables without learning anything new: upload, seal and share.

useCases.title: Use cases
useCases.sub: Where a unique, unalterable document makes the difference.

blocks.p: Seal the quote before sending it. If the client returns a “tweaked” version, verification exposes it in seconds.
After signing, seal the final PDF. Any later modification invalidates the seal and becomes evident.
Designs, manuscripts or reports: prove your delivery existed with that exact content on a specific date, with a public verification link.

blocks.h: How to make your PDF tamper-proof
blocks.p: A normal PDF can be edited in seconds. The robust way to protect it is not password-locking it (that breaks), but registering its SHA-256 fingerprint: a unique identifier that changes entirely if a single byte is altered. With TRAMPTO it's automatic.
An e-signature answers “who signed this?”. TRAMPTO answers both questions at once: “is this still what was sealed?” and “who sealed it and when?”. They're complementary.

blocks.h: Why your document is unique from its hash
blocks.p: SHA-256 produces 2²⁵⁶ possible fingerprints: more than there are atoms in the observable universe. The odds of two different documents sharing a fingerprint are, in practice, zero.

faq.sub: The essentials about sealing and verification.

items.q: What does sealing a document with TRAMPTO mean?
items.a: It computes your document's SHA-256 cryptographic fingerprint and registers it with a unique Seal ID and a date. From that hash on, your document is unique on the internet: if a single bit changes, the fingerprint no longer matches and it's detected.

items.q: Is my document uploaded to a server?
items.a: No. Sealing and fingerprint computation happen on your device. We only store the SHA-256 fingerprint, the file name, the Seal ID and the date — never the document's content.
TRAMPTO proves the document's integrity and records who sealed it and when. It complements electronic signatures; for qualified-signature requirements, combine it with a recognized signature.

items.q: How does someone verify my document?
items.a: With the public verification link (/v/{hash}) you get when sealing, or by uploading the sealed PDF to the Verify tab. In seconds it confirms whether it's authentic and unaltered.
You can seal your first documents for free. With the Pro plan (€1.99/month) you seal without limits; the actual charge is always in euros via Stripe.
